readings.reading: Each single coloured cell's Chebyshev distance from the grid centre picks a ring; the output is concentric square rings around the centre, each ring painted the colour of the single cell at that distance.
readings.why: on every pair the sources occupy distinct distances 0..(n-1)/2 and every output cell equals the colour of the source at its own distance

readings.reading: Each isolated pixel grows into the full square ring, centred on the grid centre, that passes through it (ring index = Chebyshev distance of the pixel from the centre); the rings together cover the whole grid.
readings.why: the output cell at Chebyshev distance r from the centre has the colour of the unique input pixel at distance r

readings.reading: Each scattered cell lies on one concentric square ring around the grid centre (ring index = Chebyshev distance from the centre); the whole ring is painted that cell's colour, giving nested square rings.
readings.why: exactly one non-background cell lies on each ring; the output is constant on each ring and equals that cell's colour

readings.reading: Each coloured cell becomes a full square ring centred on the grid centre, at radius equal to its Chebyshev distance from the centre; the rings fill the whole grid.
readings.why: every radius 0..R has exactly one coloured cell, so each output cell takes the colour of the cell whose radius equals its own

readings.reading: Each single coloured cell on the 7 background becomes a full square ring centred on the grid centre, at that cell's Chebyshev distance from the centre; the result is a set of concentric rings, one per mark.
readings.why: on every pair each ring distance 0..r_max holds exactly one mark, and every output cell has the colour of the mark at its own Chebyshev distance from the centre

readings.reading: Objects fall to the grid edge by shape: hollow rectangles (rings) slide straight up to the top, plus/cross shapes slide straight down to the bottom, stacking on whatever they meet in their columns.
readings.why: every object keeps its shape and columns; rings end touching the top or a ring above them, crosses end touching the bottom or a cross below them

readings.reading: Shapes with a hole (hollow rectangles) slide straight up and solid plus/cross shapes slide straight down, each until it hits the grid border or another shape already stacked there.
readings.why: every holed object ends touching the top border or a holed object above it; every cross ends touching the bottom border or a cross below it; columns and shapes are kept

readings.reading: Hollow rectangular outlines fall to the top border and solid crosses fall to the bottom border, each keeping its column and shape and stacking on objects already settled in the same direction (the two groups pass through each other).
readings.why: every object keeps shape, colour and columns; outlines end touching the top border or another outline, crosses touching the bottom border or another cross

readings.reading: Closed-loop objects (with a hole) slide straight up and crosses/open shapes slide straight down; each group stacks like gravity, ignoring the other group.
readings.why: every object keeps shape and column; hollow ones end at the top, the others at the bottom

readings.reading: Hollow rectangular rings slide straight up and cross/plus shapes slide straight down, each in its own columns, until they hit the border or an object already settled (stacking).
readings.why: every object keeps its shape and columns; rings end touching the top or a ring above, crosses end touching the bottom or a cross below

readings.reading: Every coloured cell with no orthogonally adjacent coloured cell (a lone cell under 4-connectivity) turns from 2 to 1.
readings.why: exactly the colour-2 cells with no 2 among their 4 orthogonal neighbours become 1; diagonal contact does not count (so 'markers' is too strict); colour 0 is used explicitly because in one pair 2 is the most common colour

readings.reading: Every 2-cell that has no orthogonal (4-neighbour) non-background neighbour becomes 1; diagonal contact does not count.
readings.why: exactly the non-background cells with no 4-neighbour of non-background colour change, 2 -> 1

readings.reading: Every red cell that has no red cell orthogonally adjacent (diagonal contact allowed) turns blue (1); all else unchanged.
readings.why: the 4-connected singleton 2-cells are exactly the cells that become 1; no other cell changes

readings.reading: Red cells with no orthogonal red neighbour turn blue (1); all other cells stay.
readings.why: exactly the non-zero cells without a 4-neighbour of their colour change, 2 -> 1 (diagonal contact does not count; in two pairs 2 is the most common colour, so the row uses px, not cell)

readings.reading: Every 2 cell with no 4-neighbour of non-zero colour (diagonal contact allowed) turns 1; all other cells stay.
readings.why: exactly the non-zero cells without an orthogonal non-zero neighbour change, 2 -> 1 (written with px and C > 0 because in pair 3 colour 2 is the most common colour)

readings.reading: The grid holds several same-size squares with an 8 border and a 2-pattern inside, among 8 noise; all squares share one inner pattern except one, and the output is that odd square cut out.
readings.why: on every pair exactly one square's interior pattern is unique and the output equals that square cut from the input

readings.reading: Several equal-size square boxes framed in 8 with a 2/8 interior pattern lie in noisy 1/8 background; all boxes share one interior pattern except one, and the output is that odd box cut out (frame included).
readings.why: the output equals the one box whose interior 2-pattern occurs only once among the boxes

readings.reading: Several 8-framed squares hold a pattern of 2s; all but one share the same 2-pattern. Output is the framed square whose 2-pattern is unique.
readings.why: exactly one colour-2 component has a shape no other 2-component has; its box grown by one cell is the 8-framed square that equals the output

readings.reading: Among several 8-framed squares with red patterns inside (noise 8 pixels around), output the one square whose red pattern is unique.
readings.why: red cells cluster per square (gap <= 2); exactly one cluster has a pattern no other cluster has, and its box grown by 1 is the square

readings.reading: Several 8-bordered squares hold a pattern of 2s; all but one share the same 2-pattern. Cut out the square whose 2-pattern is unique, including its 8 border.
readings.why: on every training pair exactly one 2-component has a shape no other 2-component has, and its box grown by one cell is exactly the output square (plain 'odd' fails because noise 8s touch the squares)

readings.reading: Four same-coloured cells that form the corners of a rectangle get the cells strictly inside that rectangle filled with 2.
readings.why: every cell strictly inside a rectangle whose four corners are coloured cells becomes 2; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Four same-colour corner pixels mark a rectangle; the cells strictly inside it are filled with 2.
readings.why: every cell strictly between the rows and columns of a 4-corner rectangle becomes 2; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Four same-coloured (4) cells mark the corners of a rectangle; the cells strictly inside that rectangle are filled with 2.
readings.why: every cell strictly inside a rectangle whose four corners are marker cells becomes 2; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Four yellow cells mark the corners of a rectangle; its strict interior is filled with red (2).
readings.why: every cell strictly inside a four-corner rectangle becomes 2; corners and everything else unchanged

readings.reading: Each set of four 4-cells at the corners of a rectangle gets its strict interior filled with 2.
readings.why: exactly the background cells strictly inside a rectangle with 4 at all four corners become 2

readings.reading: One panel holds a small line pattern (vertical and horizontal coloured lines with fixed crossing priority), separated by 5s from a panel whose edges carry 4-markers; the output is the marker panel's size with the pattern's lines redrawn on the rows and columns the 4s mark.
readings.why: on every pair the output's line count, colours and crossing colours equal the template's, and line positions equal the 4-marked rows and columns

readings.reading: A 5-separated half shows a small line lattice (vertical and horizontal coloured lines with a fixed crossing precedence); the other half has 4-markers on its borders giving line positions. The output is the marker half with the lattice redrawn: verticals at the marked columns, horizontals at the marked rows, colours in the same order and the same line on top at crossings.
readings.why: each output column with an edge marker is a full line of the matching lattice colour, each marked row likewise, with the lattice's crossing rule; all else 0

readings.verb: redraw legend lines at marked positions
readings.reading: A 5-separator splits a small legend (a lattice of coloured vertical and horizontal lines, partly covered by a 5 block) from a 4-marker panel; output is the marker panel redrawn: 4s at the panel edges mark line positions, and the k-th vertical/horizontal line takes the legend's k-th vertical/horizontal line colour with the legend's over/under layering at crossings.
readings.why: legend has as many vertical/horizontal lines as the marker panel marks; output lines sit exactly at marked rows/columns with legend colours and layering

readings.reading: A small key block (left of the grey separator) shows a lattice of coloured vertical and horizontal lines with set crossings; the output is the marker panel redrawn with that lattice, lines placed at the rows/columns marked by the yellow edge markers.
readings.why: line counts in the key equal the marked row/column counts; all other output cells are 0

readings.reading: A small line pattern (vertical and horizontal coloured lines with a fixed crossing priority) sits in the 5-bounded corner; the other panel has 4-markers on its edges marking rows and columns. The output is that panel redrawn with the pattern's lines placed at the marked rows and columns, same colours, order and crossing priority.
readings.why: output size equals the marker panel; full-length lines appear exactly on the marked rows/columns with the pattern's colours and crossing order

readings.reading: The input is two equal squares: an 8 mask and a coloured pattern. The output is a block grid: block (i,j) is the mask shape painted in the colour of pattern cell (i,j), or empty when that cell is background.
readings.why: every output block is either empty or the mask shape in exactly the colour of the corresponding pattern cell

readings.reading: The input splits into two equal halves: a colour pattern and a mask drawn in 8. The output is the Kronecker product: each coloured cell of the pattern becomes a copy of the mask in that colour, each 0 cell an empty block.
readings.why: output block (i,j) = mask with 8 replaced by pattern[i][j] (all 0 if pattern[i][j] = 0)

readings.reading: The input is two equal square halves: one is an 8 mask, the other a colour pattern. Output is their Kronecker product: each coloured cell becomes a copy of the mask painted in that colour, each background cell an empty block.
readings.why: every k×k output block is the mask in the colour of the matching pattern cell, or all background

readings.reading: The input splits into a shape half (8 on 0) and a colour half; each coloured cell of the colour half becomes a copy of the shape in that colour (Kronecker product), empty cells become empty blocks.
readings.why: output size = colours size x shape size; every block is the shape in one colour or empty

readings.reading: The input is two equal panels: an 8 mask and a colour pattern. The output is their Kronecker product: each coloured cell of the colour panel becomes a copy of the 8 mask in that colour, each empty cell an empty block.
readings.why: output is n*n blocks of n*n; block (i,j) is the mask in colour layout(i,j), or empty if layout(i,j) is 0

readings.reading: An 8 legend panel shows small 3x3 shapes, each in its own colour. Each 5x5 box is swapped by the legend: a 2-box with a 1-pattern becomes a solid box in the colour whose legend shape matches the pattern (up to rotation/reflection); a solid coloured box becomes a 2-box with that colour's legend shape drawn in 1.
readings.why: on every pair each box's output is determined by the legend lookup of its pattern or its colour

readings.reading: A legend panel (8 background) pairs small 3x3 shapes with colours. Each 5x5 box carrying a 1-pattern on 2 becomes solid in the colour whose legend shape matches the pattern; each solid-colour box becomes the 2 box with that colour's legend shape drawn in 1.
readings.why: every box is swapped between its pattern form and its colour form through the legend

readings.verb: swap block between pattern and legend colour
readings.reading: Left side holds 5x5 blocks, each either solid colour c or a 2-frame with a 3x3 pattern of 1s; the 8-panel legend shows one 3x3 pattern per colour. A solid c block becomes a 2-frame with legend-c's pattern in 1s; a patterned block becomes solid in the colour whose legend pattern matches it up to rotation/reflection.
readings.why: each block's 3x3 interior pattern corresponds to exactly one legend colour (up to D4), and solid blocks map to their colour's exact legend shape

readings.reading: An 8-panel holds a legend of small coloured 3x3 shapes. Each 5x5 red box with a blue pattern becomes a solid box of the legend colour whose shape matches the pattern (up to rotation/reflection); each solid coloured box becomes a red box with that colour's legend shape drawn in blue.
readings.why: each box is replaced in place, the legend panel and background never change

readings.reading: An 8-background legend holds small coloured 3x3 shapes. Each 2-framed box whose interior 1-pattern matches a legend shape (up to rotation) becomes a solid block of that shape's colour; each solid single-colour block becomes a 2-framed box whose interior 1-pattern is that colour's legend shape.
readings.why: every 5x5 box swaps between pattern form and solid form via the legend; legend and background never change

readings.reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent 2-cells (a domino) gets a 3 outline drawn in all background cells around it; single 2-cells are left alone.
readings.why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a two-cell straight object become 3; lone cells get nothing

readings.reading: Each domino (two orthogonally adjacent 2s) gets a ring of 3 around it on the surrounding background cells; single 2s are untouched.
readings.why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a 2-cell orthogonal domino become 3

readings.reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent red cells (a domino) gets a one-cell green (3) outline around it; isolated red cells are left alone.
readings.why: the background cells 8-adjacent to a two-cell orthogonal red object are exactly the cells that become 3

readings.reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent red cells gets a green (3) outline in the surrounding background cells; single red cells are untouched.
readings.why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a 2-cell domino become 3

readings.reading: Every pair of adjacent 2 cells (a domino) gets a 3 halo on all background cells around it; single 2 cells stay as they are.
readings.why: exactly the background 8-neighbours of size-2 components become 3

readings.reading: A key row of k colours sits above a slanted staircase band of 5s; the band is recoloured in steps of k rows along its diagonal, each step painted as nested L-shaped layers from the step's leading corner using key[0..k-1], the last key colour filling the rest.
readings.why: every 5 cell is replaced by a key colour following the repeating nested-L layer pattern; no other cell changes

readings.verb: paint diagonal band with cycling key
readings.reading: A key row gives a colour sequence; each diagonal band of 5 is a stack of WxW squares stepping one cell diagonally from its top end. The squares are painted in order with the key colours cycling, later squares overwriting earlier ones, so the band shows nested L-strokes and ends in a solid square.
readings.why: every 5 cell takes the colour of the last (highest k) band square containing it; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Each diagonal staircase band of 5s is coloured as nested L-shaped layers starting from its top end (corner at the top row's outer end, arms along the top row and down the outer column), layer k taking key colour k mod n from the key row; the leftover cap at the far end takes the last layer's colour.
readings.why: every 5 cell gets key[k mod n] for its layer k; key row and background unchanged

readings.reading: A colour sequence at the top paints each grey diagonal band in nested chevron layers: the band's leading row and edge get the first colour, the next layer the second, and so on, the innermost layer continuing to the band's end.
readings.why: only 5-cells change; each becomes a key colour determined by its layer depth

readings.reading: A key row of colours sits at the top; each diagonal 5 band is recoloured in nested L-shaped layers starting at its square-cut end, layer k taking key colour k mod len(key), with the far-end square block all one layer colour.
readings.why: only 5 cells change; each takes the key colour of its L-layer index from the band's starting corner, cycling through the key
